Using the board

  1. Start on Tickets — tonight’s board, already drafted. Read it top to bottom: 👟 The Brace, 🧤 The Goal Line, 🥅 Top Bin. The card at the top is the running season ledger. The View chips filter to one kind at a time.
  2. Check the lock line before you act on anything. Anything still projected can change as team news lands; the ✓ arrives with the published XI. The board re-reads the results feed every few minutes: goals, red cards and full time settle themselves on the card.
  3. Open Players to see the field the board drafted from. Every player who cleared the pool gate, one card each. Sort by model score, shortest price, confirmed first, team or name, or search.
  4. Use Research to see why. One row per player: xG, minutes, the defence he faces, and our chance against the price. Switch the View to Goals for the team-totals model behind the Goal Line. Click a name for the breakdown; + puts him on the slip tray, which follows you to every tab.
  5. Know how a pick settles. An anytime goal counts in normal time and stoppage time, not extra time, and own goals do not count. A player who does not play is refunded. Goal Line legs settle on the final score.
👟
The BraceOur pick of the day, one ticket at 2u. Of the starters already on the board at +250 or shorter, the man whose xG sits furthest above his price gets both units on one slip instead of a 1u single. Anytime goalscorer. Board players only.
🧤
The Goal LineOne parlay a day on goals, not scorers: game totals, team totals and both teams to score, one leg per match. The slate sets the size: one leg on a one-match day, two on 2-5 matches, three on 6-11, four on 12 or more. Each leg is a line our goals model rates most likely to land that still pays -250 or better.
🥅
Top BinEvery confirmed starter we rate 45% or better to score (two a match at most), each a straight 1u single.

Operator console (hidden from normal viewers). Type a number per player — prices update live and save in this browser. Hit Download to bake them into a fresh page to share; that shared file is a fixed snapshot.

Operator log

Oct 10 · who scoresTop Bin now ranks every confirmed starter by his chance to score: the book’s price averaged with the scorer model (team goals expected × share of team xG × minutes × penalties). Only players at 45% or better make the card, at most two a match and no nightly limit: a thin slate posts fewer picks instead of padding, a deep one posts them all. The season tracker is restated under this rule from Aug 27.
Sep 17 · top 8The card is now the top 8 confirmed starters as straight 1u singles, plus a 🍱 lunch special and a 🌃 nightcap, ranked by the new scorer model (team goals expected × share of team xG × minutes) blended with the price. Anchors and screamers are retired. The season tracker is restated: every night since Aug 27 re-run under this system at the prices that night; the record the old board actually posted is kept in the repo.
Aug 26 · live resultsThe board now re-reads the results feed every three minutes. Goals, goal minutes, red cards and full time settle themselves on the card, and the tickets tab grades tonight as they land. What it deliberately does not do: it does not re-draft (the draft engine is still Python-side), it does not run a second grader, and it never infers full time from a clock — only the feed writes a final. Anything it cannot match to a board name is left alone rather than guessed at.
Aug 26 · team newsConfirmed line-ups are wired. The draft now runs off the published XI, so a name on a slip started the match. Today’s slate was thin enough that four anchors would not fit the pool, so it drafted the largest count that did — one — rather than padding the card with names the gate rejected.
Aug 24 · forkThe soccer room is a seam-for-seam fork of the baseball board, not a rewrite — same layout, same card anatomy, same draft engine. What is not carried over is said so out loud: the Builder’s letter grade is off until there are graded soccer nights to fit it on.
